newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Two groups to bid for Israel's Hapoalim.
newsitem.headline: Two groups to bid for Israel's Hapoalim.

text.p: Two groups have registered to bid for a controlling stake in Israel's Bank Hapoalim, MI Holdings, the company selling the state-owned bank said on Thursday.
The deadline for submitting offers to purchase a stake in Israel's largest commercial bank is April 18.
The first group, led by U.S. banker Jeffrey Keil, includes Israeli entrepreneur Eliezer Fishman and investment bank Lazard Freres.
The second group, which formally registered in March, is a consortium headed by the U.S.-Israeli entrepreneur Ted Arison.

The Arison group includes Claridge Israel, an investment company controlled by Charles Bronfman; U.S. investor Michael Steinhardt and his partner Shlomo Topor, Israel's Dankner Group; Hyperion, a U.S. bank investment fund and U.S. insurance entrepreneur Len Abramson.
Both groups have made a deposit of $40 million required to bid for a stake in the bank.

The Israeli government controls 78 percent of Hapoalim with the remainder traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange. It aims to sell between 25 percent and 69.3 percent through the tender which it hopes to complete by mid-August.
Claridge had led an earlier bid for control of Hapoalim but dropped out. In March, MI Holdings announced a new tender.
